title: FluencyCraft Beginner - Day 05
why_important: Courteous invitations build friendly community relationships.

word_of_the_day.meaning: Visit someone informally for a short time
word_of_the_day.usage: Please drop by our home for tea.

questions.question: Day 5 Scenario (Polite Social Manners): Select the natural English phrasing when The store vendor is ordering food at a restaurant yesterday afternoon:

options.a: Could we please see the menu and order starters?
options.b: Menu giving order doing.
options.c: Menu giving order doing. yesterday
options.d: I am ordering food at a restaurant right now.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Could we please see the menu and order starters?".

questions.question: Day 5 Practice (Polite Social Manners): When talking about asking for item weight price (on weekends), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'Our neighbor'?

options.a: I am asking for item weight price right now.
options.b: How much are these organic apples per kilo?
options.c: Apples kg how much cost?
options.d: Apples kg how much cost? yesterday

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "How much are these organic apples per kilo?".

questions.question: Day 5 Practice (Polite Social Manners): When talking about preparing breakfast for family (on weekends), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The delivery executive'?

options.b: He is prepare breakfast fisily.
options.c: I am prepare breakfast family.
options.d: I prepared breakfast for my family this morning.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I prepared breakfast for my family this morning.".

questions.question: Day 5 Practice (Polite Social Manners): When talking about inquiring about doctor appointment (twice a week), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My sister'?

options.b: I am inquiring about doctor appointment right now.
options.c: Doctor meeting wanted for fever.
options.d: I need to consult a doctor regarding a mild fever.

questions.explanation:

questions.question: Day 5 Vocabulary (Polite Social Manners): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'pick out'?

options.a: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: Carefully choose specific items from a group.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'pick out' means: carefully choose specific items from a group. Example: "Could you help me pick out the best mangos?"

questions.question: Day 5 Vocabulary (Polite Social Manners): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'call off'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: Cancel a planned event or meeting.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
'call off' means: cancel a planned event or meeting. Example: "They had to call off the afternoon presentation."

questions.question: Day 5 Terms (Polite Social Manners): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'fill out':

options.a: Complete an official form.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'fill out' means: complete an official form. Example: "Please fill out this registration form."

questions.question: Day 5 Vocabulary (Polite Social Manners): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'follow up'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:

'follow up' means: check progress on a prior matter. Example: "I will follow up with the team regarding the report."

questions.question:
Day 5 Translation Scenario 1 (Polite Social Manners):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.c: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.d: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.

questions.question:
Day 5 Translation Scenario 2 (Polite Social Manners):

Telugu: "సాయంత్రం మా ఇంటికి రండి, టీ తాగుదాం."
(Literal attempt: "Evening my house come, tea drink.")

options.a: Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: I am needing to evening my house come, tea drink.
options.d: Evening my house come, tea drink.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together."

Use 'drop by our home' for informal invitations.

questions.question:
Day 5 Translation Scenario 3 (Polite Social Manners):

Telugu: "ఈ ఒప్పందంలో కొన్ని మార్పులు చేస్తే బాగుంటుంది."
(Literal attempt: "In agreement some changes if do good.")

options.a: I am needing to in agreement some changes if do good.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: In agreement some changes if do good.
options.d: It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement."

Use executive diplomacy 'It would be advantageous to...'.

questions.question:
Day 5 Translation Scenario 4 (Polite Social Manners):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.b: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.c: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.
